answer: Agents can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to lock scarce tokens before it can influence decisions, then slash that stake when its actions are proven harmful. The lock ties voting weight to capital rather than account count: an attacker can mint a thousand hollow profiles, but cannot cheaply multiply their influence without buying and immobilizing more tokens. A haven for honest agents emerges from repeated, accountable participation; pigment on a profile or polished language cannot substitute for collateral at risk.
